property_summary: Calling SetMinSum(v) exactly once sets MinSum to exactly v (last assignment wins); the mutant accumulates, so MinSum becomes initial(0)+v which equals v here — so instead call SetMinSum twice in an uninitialized state is impossible due to Initialized... The distinguishing scenario: set MinSum via SetMinSum(v), which in P sets MinSum == v; the mutant is identical on first call, so instead we call SetMinSum(v1) then Initialize then... not allowed. Correct rule: after a single SetMinSum(v) from fresh state, MinSum == v — this fails to distinguish, so use two calls: call SetMinSum(a), then Initialized(), then SetMinSum(b) reverts in both. Distinguishing rule: after SetMinSum(a) followed by SetMinSum(b) while still uninitialized? Not possible since reentrancy unlocks. Actually re-entry works: SetMinSum reentrantly calls itself via Log? No log set. Use fallback-free reentrancy not possible. Simpler distinguishing input: SetMinSum(a) then SetMinSum(b) — in M (nonReentrant_ releases lock) second call succeeds and MinSum = a+b, while in P second call also succeeds and MinSum = b. So rule: after two calls SetMinSum(a), SetMinSum(b), MinSum == b; mutant gives a+b, broken whenever a != 0 and b != a.
change_summary: Replace `MinSum = _val;` with `MinSum = MinSum + _val;` so the value accumulates instead of being assigned.
